newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: China demand to force up veg oil price - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: China demand to force up veg oil price - Oil World.

text.p: China's emergence as a buyer of vegetable oils since 1994 has marked a significant new phase in the market, raising the forecast price of rape oil in Rotterdam in the 10 years to 2003 to average $580 a tonne, Oil World said.
The average price in the 21-year period to 1993 was $490.
Oil World said China's import demand would probably keep rising, making another price rise after 2003 likely.

The consumption of the 17 major oils and fats was forecast to rise to 106.6 million tonnes by 2000 from 92.5 million in 1995. This should further increase to 120 million tonnes in 2005 and to nearly 135 million by 2010.
The majority of this increase will result from developing countries, where population growth is expected to remain high and per capita usage of oils and fats is still low.
Helping to tighten the supply/demand balance is the fact that total world crop area cannot be expanded commensurately with the growth of demand for all crops.

Oil World cited other factors including the relatively high price for grains, which will mean oilseed prices will have to remain strong to successfully compete for land, and slowing palm oil production over the next decade as keeping the market tight. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
